chunks.title: Westinghouse iGen12000DFc Review
chunks.text: Westinghouse iGen12000DFc Review — The verdict: Out of stock — that is the verdict that matters right now. The iGen12000DFc was $1,899 when last verified on Nov 20, 2026, and the listing shows it out of stock with no arrival date. Do not pay a markup for it from a third-party listing while the Walmart listing is gone; the Pulsar G12KBN at $739 below is the same 12,000-peak class for $1,160 less, and it is in stock. When it is in stock, it is the quiet big inverter in this roster: 12,000 peak watts on gas with clean power under 3% THD, remote start, and a CO sensor, at 189 pounds — one of the lightest in its class. Buyers give it 4.8 stars from 2,293 ratings, and the newest review, from a buyer who purchased November 14, says it “fired up on first attempt with gas” with every outlet working. The honest catches: one buyer at 7,600 feet elevation found it “does not carry nearly the output load that it advertised” and is waiting on a high-altitude kit, and at $1,899 it is the most expensive generator in this batch.

chunks.title: Westinghouse iGen12000DFc Review
chunks.text: Westinghouse iGen12000DFc Review — Performance in real use: The 457cc engine makes 12,000 peak / 9,000 running watts on gasoline and 11,000 / 8,100 on propane, with a 7.9-gallon tank and up to 19 hours at 25% load on gas — about 0.42 gallons per hour, one of the better fuel-efficiency figures in its class. At 64 dBA it is quieter than the open-frame generators in this batch, and under 3% THD means sensitive electronics are safe on it. The control panel carries 4 AC outlets including a 50-amp outlet, and it is transfer-switch ready. Remote start comes with a key fob. Buyers report it starting first try and running a house; one buyer at high altitude reports reduced output and is installing the high-altitude kit.

chunks.title: Westinghouse iGen12000DFc Review
chunks.text: Westinghouse iGen12000DFc Review — Setup: Recoil, electric, and remote start — the key fob is included. At 189 pounds it is light for its class, but still a two-person lift or a ramp job. Break it in before the outage: run it at varying loads for the first hours, change the oil on schedule, and test every outlet — the newest buyer did exactly that and reports all outlets working. If you live at altitude, order the high-altitude kit with it; the standard jetting loses output above roughly 7,000 feet.

chunks.title: Westinghouse iGen5000 Review
chunks.text: Westinghouse iGen5000 Review — The verdict: Buy it if you want the 5,000-watt Westinghouse inverter for $50 less than the CO-sensor version and you do not need the sensor. At $849 it is the cheapest 5,000-watt inverter in this batch, with the same 224cc engine, the same 3.4-gallon tank, and the same remote start as the iGen5000c. Buyers give the listing 4.7 stars from 16,250 ratings — a family aggregate, so read it as the iGen5000 line's record, not this exact unit's — and the words that keep showing up are “easy set up,” “very quiet,” and “remote start. ” One buyer: “I just received my generator and it worked as advertised. ” The honest catches: there is no CO sensor on this model — if the sensor matters to you, the iGen5000c is $899 — and the review count is shared across the family, so the 16,250 figure overstates this exact listing's base. At 104.7 pounds it is not a one-person carry. If you want propane, the Champion 201319 at $999 is the move.

chunks.title: Westinghouse iGen5000 Review
chunks.text: Westinghouse iGen5000 Review — Who it's for: Anyone who wants the 5,000-watt Westinghouse inverter at the lowest price in the batch and does not need a CO sensor or propane. Skip it if the CO sensor matters to you: the iGen5000c is $50 more. Skip it if you need propane: this model is gas-only.

chunks.title: Westinghouse iGen5000 Review
chunks.text: Westinghouse iGen5000 Review — Performance in real use: The 224cc engine makes 5,000 peak / 3,900 running watts, with a 3.4-gallon tank and up to 18 hours at 25% load — about 0.19 gallons per hour. At 52 dBA it is quiet for its class, and under 3% THD means sensitive electronics are safe on it. The control panel carries 3 AC outlets including the TT-30R RV outlet, plus a digital display. Remote start comes with a key fob — buyers call it out by name: “key fob works great,” “very happy with generator. ” One buyer notes the electric start did not work until the battery charged overnight — charge the battery before the first start.

chunks.title: Westinghouse iGen5000 Review
chunks.text: Westinghouse iGen5000 Review — Setup: Recoil, electric, and remote start — the key fob is included. Charge the battery overnight before the first electric start: one buyer reports it would not start electronically until the battery charged. At 104.7 pounds, plan a ramp or a second person to load it. Break it in before the outage and test the remote start from inside the RV — the fob is the feature buyers praise most.
